findings.reproduction: Import frozen3e consumer; capture dependency_pins[D]. Privately mock sha(D) to f*64 and use a fake import loader callback only. dependency_pins changes to f*64; audit_numeric reaches exec_module and returns the fake numerical result. A later Pins.check against the original SHA rejects. No D source was changed or actually executed.
findings.effect: No demonstrated false final acceptance: the post-compute initial-pin check remains effective. The defect permits changed/unreviewed dependency code to execute before rejection, and preparation API can refresh its expected digest.
findings.expected: Seal the independently reviewed final D source SHA in the initial dependency inventory, validate it before spec.loader.exec_module and before compute, retain after-import/after-compute/final pin checks. Do not seal oldd85; root reported corrected a7b079 pending separate numeric review.
findings.recommendation: Capture/declare the accepted D SHA once; dependency_pins must return that immutable expectation. audit_numeric must compare current D bytes to the initially request-bound/accepted digest before import.

findings.problem: Cache head NPY full-file hashes are re-established from current files rather than rebound to the already fixed complete.head weight/bias SHA declarations.

Add standard complete.head weight_file/weight_sha256/bias_file/bias_sha256, rebind all dependent marker/admission/identity/producer/launch/exit JSONs, and confirm baseline. Change one padding space in synthetic head_weight.npy header to a tab; shape,dtype and every raw FP32 head byte stay identical. findings.effect: An admitted cache head file can drift from its externally bound complete manifest while the result consumer reports metadata provenance rechecked. The demonstrated numerical head values remain unchanged; this is a file-integrity/provenance failure, not a claim of wrong AUC.

findings.recommendation: Use the existing complete head SHA declarations as Pins.add expectations; never refresh them from sha(hp). Add private padding-only drift regression.
